0.long_answer: Mucolipidosis type I (Sialidosis) is one of the disorders historically grouped under mucolipidoses, a group of inherited metabolic disorders that affect the turnover of various cellular materials. However, a more modern biochemical classification has redefined type I (Sialidosis) as a glycoproteinosis. This reclassification is based on its underlying biochemical defect, which involves a deficiency in the enzyme alpha-N-acetyl neuraminidase (sialidase) that leads to the abnormal accumulation of glycoproteins. Thus, within the broader scheme of inherited metabolic disorders, ML I (Sialidosis) specifically belongs to the glycoproteinoses.
